title: Chapter 25: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

blocks.content: The primary objective of TRAI is to create and nurture conditions for growth of telecommunications in India in a manner and at a pace which will enable India to play a leading role in the emerging global information society.

rows: Regulation of telecom services and tariff determination
Adjudication of disputes and hearing appeals

items: TDSAT was created via the TRAI (Amendment) Act, 2000, specifically separating regulatory functions from judicial dispute resolution.
TRAI's recommendations are advisory in nature and are not binding on the Central Government.
Members of TRAI are ineligible for further employment under the Central or State Governments after demitting office.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI is a statutory body established on February 20, 1997, under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
The TRAI (Amendment) Act of 2000 established the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) to divest adjudicatory functions from TRAI.
The body consists of a Chairperson, not more than two whole-time members, and not more than two part-time members appointed by the Central Government.
Members hold office for a term of three years or until attaining the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
TRAI aims to provide a fair and transparent policy environment that promotes a level playing field and facilitates fair competition in telecommunications.
